findings.description: The URL filter only rejects regex matches whose captured path contains `//`, but URLs commonly produce a later partial match without the scheme slashes. For `https://example.com/x.js:8080`, the regex can match `example.com/x.js:8080`; that captured path does not contain `//`, so it is counted as a citation despite the new documented rule and RG-20 expectation that URLs are not path citations.
findings.failure_mode: Clean-fixture reviews that mention URLs with file-like paths and ports can be scored as false positives, and defect fixtures can receive bogus credit from a URL rather than an actual file citation.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject URL-derived partial matches by adding a left-boundary guard that prevents matching immediately after `://` or a slash-slash URL host, or inspect the surrounding text around the match for a URL scheme/authority before accepting the citation. Add a regression case for `https://example.com/x.js:8080` specifically.

findings.cross_file_justification: The grader diff changes citation semantics (grader_version 1.1.0 -> 1.1.1: trailer stripped from the body, JSON-adjacent bare :N excluded, backtick/bold-wrapped paths bind their own line, no newline-crossing continuations, URL skip). The sprint.md hunk in the same diff keeps the Replay A/B acceptance criterion marked met, citing a2a/sprint-250/replay-ab-rerun.md, whose 27-slot per-case numbers were produced at bf988a43 by grader 1.1.0 (per the implementation report: e612fa2d = 1.1.0, the 1.1.1 changes come from review run 1 n40-n42, after the re-run).
findings.description: The pre-registered gate ('no gold case loses recall; a drop blocks the sprint') is measured by this grader, and the measuring instrument changed after the measurement. The 1.1.1 changes are not monotonic: stripping the trailer, excluding JSON numbers, and refusing newline continuations can only remove credit, but binding `path`:N / **path**:N to its own line can ADD credit to either arm (under 1.1.0 those bound to the previous path or credited nothing). Reviewer output routinely wraps paths in backticks, so per-arm counts on audit-pr-02 / audit-pr-05 (27/27 and 26/27, both at the gate edge) can move in either direction. Nothing in the diff or report shows both arms re-graded with 1.1.1.
findings.failure_mode: The recorded 'gate passes' and the [x] on the Sprint 3 recall AC may not hold under the grader that is actually being merged. If a re-grade shows an after-arm loss, the pre-registered revert rule should have fired and the CLAUDE.loa.md / rationale decisions are unsupported; if it shows a before-arm gain, same outcome. Either way the binding condition in a2a/sprint-249/engineer-feedback.md ('two-arm re-baseline before the cycle PR merges') is unmet for the shipped grader.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run recall-vs-defects.sh 1.1.1 over the saved before/after review files for every gold case (deterministic, no model calls), diff the per-case detected/missed lists against the 1.1.0 report, and append the result to replay-ab-rerun.md before merge. If any case changes, apply the pre-registered rule. Add the grader_version to the A/B report header so instrument/measurement drift is visible next time.

findings.description: The number-boundary guard `(?![A-Za-z0-9-])` is applied only to comma continuations, not to the first RNG, and it lists only the ASCII hyphen while RNG accepts the en dash. So `a.sh:12-2026-10-05`, `a.sh:12 - 40 rows were dropped` (same line, RG-19 only tests the newline form) and `a.sh:12, 2026–10–05` (en dashes) all parse as ranges 12..2026 or 12..40. The header comment claims 'a continuation or range ... must end at a number boundary (no dates)', which the range path does not implement.
findings.failure_mode: A wide accidental range credits every planted defect in that file whose anchor falls inside it (the ±3 check is `not (b < s-3 or a > s+3)`), inflating recall on defect fixtures and masking real misses in the A/B gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same negative lookahead after the first RNG (and after `bare`), and include the en dash in the lookahead class: `(?![A-Za-z0-9\-–])`. Add a one-line RG case for `a.sh:12 - 40 rows` and an en-dash date.

findings.description: The JSON-punctuation lookbehind set (`"'{}[]*`) was added to both branches of the bare alternative, including the one guarding the `head|base` prefix. A quoted or bracketed `"head:40"` / `[head:40]` therefore no longer binds to the last path, a regression from the 1.1.0 behaviour the header still documents. Conversely the backtick is absent from the set, so `` `rows`:40 `` or `` `"high"`:3 `` still binds a bare :N to the previous path even though the header says a bare :N 'after a quote' credits nothing.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent credit: legitimate `head:N` references in quotes lose credit, while backtick-wrapped non-path tokens followed by :N keep false credit, exactly the class of n41 false positive this change set out to remove.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the original word-boundary set for the `head|base` branch and apply the punctuation set only to the fully bare `:N` branch; add the backtick to that set. Pin both with RG cases.

findings.description: The body stripper matches `<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT.*?-->` with re.S, but the trailer reader below still uses `<!-- LOA-VERDICT (\{.*\}) -->` (exactly one space, single line). A trailer with no space, two spaces, or a line break inside the JSON is removed from the citation body but not parsed for counts, so `sev` is None and `fp` falls back to the raw citation count. Also, an unterminated `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` will strip everything up to the next `-->` anywhere in the document (re.S), silently deleting real citations.
findings.failure_mode: On a clean fixture the grader reports false positives equal to the citation count and fails the run even though the model emitted a valid-looking verdict; on a defect fixture a malformed trailer can erase citations and produce a spurious recall miss.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile the trailer pattern once (`\s*`, re.S) and use it for both the strip and the read; anchor the strip to `-->` on the same comment by forbidding `<!--` inside (`(?:(?!<!--).)*?`) or by matching only the final trailer at end of file.
